reading.body:
A founding OpenAI CTO launched Thinking Machines Lab in February 2025 to build collaborative, multimodal AI systems that work with people rather than pursuing full autonomy.

Murati's departure from OpenAI after nearly six years, including a stint as interim CEO during the November 2023 board crisis, marked a shift in focus within the AI leadership class. Her new company's stated philosophy centers on human-AI collaboration rather than systems designed for independent operation. This represents a distinct position in the market at a time when debate over AI autonomy remains unresolved.

The company's emphasis on multimodal systems and collaboration means Thinking Machines Lab operates in a narrower technical scope than the large-scale model training that dominates compute infrastructure discussion. The data provided does not specify the company's compute requirements, funding, facilities, or power consumption, making it impossible to assess how its technical approach translates to infrastructure demands. What the company prioritizes and how those priorities affect resource intensity remain separate questions.

standing.watch: What remains unresolved in the records is the litigation around OpenAI, where every listed case is filed and under docket monitoring with no development recorded yet. The tracker shows no outcome, no ruling and no settlement for any of those matters, including the cases against OpenAI OpCo, OpenAI Group PBC and OpenAI Inc. For Thinking Machines Lab, the records show a public launch but no funding, valuation or legal dispute, so its next steps are not documented here. Murati's own position is likewise unquantified, with no figures given for either company.
standing.record: The site's records tie Murati to two companies, OpenAI and Thinking Machines Lab, and to a set of lawsuits that name OpenAI entities rather than her personally. Those cases include USA Today Co., Inc. v. OpenAI Foundation, TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, and GRANT v. OPENAI INC, each marked as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded. One further case, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, names a different company and does not involve OpenAI. The pattern across the record is a career defined by OpenAI and a new venture, with legal exposure attached to OpenAI's entities and no recorded case against Thinking Machines Lab.
standing.standing: Mira Murati stands as the founder and CEO of Thinking Machines Lab, a public benefit corporation she founded in 2025 and launched publicly on February 18, 2025, focused on collaborative, multimodal AI systems. She also remains an executive of OpenAI, the San Francisco startup she joined before rising to Chief Technology Officer in May 2022. Her standing rests on that dual record: nearly six years at OpenAI, including a brief turn as interim CEO starting November 17, 2023, during the board crisis, and her departure announced September 25, 2024. The records show no funding or valuation figures for either company, so the scale of what she controls is not quantified here.

timeline.event: Becomes Chief Technology Officer of OpenAI in May 2022.
timeline.impact: Takes charge of OpenAI's research, product, and safety functions.

timeline.event: Is named interim Chief Executive Officer of OpenAI on November 17, 2023, after the board removes Sam Altman.
timeline.impact: Leads the company before Emmett Shear is named interim CEO on November 20, 2023.

timeline.event: Announces her departure from OpenAI on September 25, 2024.
timeline.impact: Ends her tenure as CTO to pursue what she described as her own exploration.

timeline.event: Launches Thinking Machines Lab publicly on February 18, 2025, as founder and CEO.
timeline.impact: Starts a new AI company focused on multimodal systems built for collaboration with people.
